facts.topic: pump.fun bonding-curve formula and initial virtual reserves
facts.claim: The pump.fun curve is constant-product (Uniswap V2-style) over virtual reserves. Live mainnet Global values decoded on 2026-10-06: initial_virtual_token_reserves = 1,073,000,000,000,000 base units (1.073B tokens at 6 decimals); initial_virtual_sol_reserves = 30,000,000,000 lamports (30 SOL); initial_real_token_reserves = 793,100,000,000,000 (793.1M tokens); token_total_supply = 1,000,000,000,000,000 (1B tokens). On each buy, virtual and real SOL rise by the same lamports and virtual and real tokens fall by the same amount. Sells do the reverse.
facts.design_relevance: A deterministic local quoter for curve trades is possible: out = f(virtual reserves). This avoids an aggregator round trip on the hot path.
facts.note: I decoded Global on 2026-10-06 and got 1073000000000000 / 30000000000 / 793100000000000 / 1000000000000000. The README describes the Uniswap-V2 virtual-reserve formula and the buy/sell reserve updates. Twelve live TradeEvents I decoded keep virtual minus real SOL at exactly 30 SOL.

facts.claim: A curve becomes complete=true at the end of the buy that brings real_token_reserves to 0, meaning all 793.1M curve tokens are sold. From the constants, real SOL at completion is about 85.005 SOL (derived) and the implied market cap is about 410.9 SOL (derived; the start is about 27.96 SOL). Three CompletePumpAmmMigrationEvents observed on 2026-10-06 each moved 206,900,000,000,000 base units (206.9M tokens) and 84,990,359,0xx lamports (about 84.99 SOL) into PumpSwap, with pool_migration_fee = 15,000,001 lamports (about 0.015 SOL). A fourth migration showed sol_amount 91,220,809 (unexplained; possibly a non-SOL quote coin).
sources: onchain getSignaturesForAddress/getTransaction for withdraw authority 39azUYFWPz3VHgKCf3VChUwbpURdCHRxjWVowf5jUJjg via https://api.mainnet-beta.solana.com, decoded with CompletePumpAmmMigrationEvent from idl/pump.json
facts.design_relevance: Gives the graduation detector its trigger, which is real_token_reserves==0 or a CompleteEvent, not a market-cap guess. Gives the expected pool depth at listing: about 85 SOL against 206.9M tokens.
facts.note: complete=true when real_token_reserves==0 matches the README, and the derived ~85.005 SOL, ~410.9 SOL cap and ~27.96 SOL start values check out. I decoded 12 more CompletePumpAmmMigrationEvents; all show 206.9M tokens, 84,990,359,056 to 84,990,360,295 lamports and a 15,000,001 lamport fee. One caveat for pool depth: at migration only about 67.41 SOL is real in the quote vault. About 17.58 SOL is virtual (see missed_critical), so effective depth is still about 84.99 SOL.

facts.claim: migrate is permissionless and idempotent, moves the completed curve into the canonical PumpSwap pool (index 0) and burns the LP. The withdraw-to-Raydium path is disabled (enable_migrate=true). Migration usually lands in the same slot as the completing buy, but it can lag: in my 4 measured cases the gaps were 0, 0, 0 and 10 slots (about 2 s). One coin was created, bought out and completed in a single transaction. Failed transactions touching the withdraw authority are common: 71 of the latest 150 in my sample, 319 of 1,000 in the researcher's. The cause is not verified.
sources: onchain getTransaction for migration and curve signatures via https://api.mainnet-beta.solana.com
facts.design_relevance: After completion the bot must switch the venue from the curve to the PumpSwap canonical pool within about 1 s. Curve buys and sells revert after complete. The bot should not spend fees calling migrate itself.
facts.original_claim: The `migrate` instruction is permissionless and idempotent. It moves a completed curve's liquidity into a canonical PumpSwap pool (index 0) and burns the LP tokens. The deprecated `withdraw` path to Raydium is disabled (enable_migrate=true on-chain). In 3 sampled graduations on 2026-10-06, migration landed 0–3 slots after the CompleteEvent, either in the same slot or 1 s later. Of the last 1,000 transactions touching the withdraw-authority account, 319 failed (for example InvalidAccountData or custom error 3012). This is consistent with competing migrate attempts, but that interpretation is not verified.

The '0-3 slots / within 1 s' timing is too tight: for mint 9jhvNe7A the CompleteEvent was at slot 453915975 and migration at slot 453915985, 10 slots and about 2 s later. The IDL also has a migrate_v2 instruction (27 accounts) that the claim does not mention.

facts.claim: The live bonding-curve FeeConfig (8Wf5Ti...) has a single tier for all market caps: lp 0 + protocol 95 bps + creator 30 bps = 1.25% per trade. Eight recent non-mayhem TradeEvents decoded on 2026-10-06 all showed fee_basis_points=95 and creator_fee_basis_points=30. Fees are computed on the SOL amount. On buys, max_sol_cost must include the fees; on sells, fees come out of the SOL proceeds. The Global account still shows fee_basis_points=95 and creator_fee_basis_points=5, but the SDK logic uses FeeConfig tiers whenever FeeConfig exists.
facts.design_relevance: The curve round trip costs about 2.5% in venue fees alone, before network costs. The strategy's simulated edge must clear this. Fees must be read from FeeConfig, not hard-coded.
facts.note: The curve FeeConfig has one tier: 0/95/30 at threshold 0, and the same values for flat, stable and exotic fees. Ten non-mayhem TradeEvents I decoded show 95/30 bps on the SOL amount. Two mayhem buys showed 0/0. Global on-chain is fee_basis_points=95 and creator_fee_basis_points=5; the README's Global example (100 bps) is stale.

facts.claim: Global.buyback_basis_points = 5000 on-chain. TradeEvents report buyback_fee as exactly 50% of the 0.95% protocol fee (for example fee 7,734,400 and buyback_fee 3,867,200). That suggests the buyback is carved out of the protocol fee, not charged on top. buy_v2 and sell_v2 require both a fee_recipient and a buyback_fee_recipient account, chosen from published lists of 8 each.

For example, fee 2,373,685 split as 1,186,843 + 1,186,842. So the buyback is carved out of the 0.95%, not added on top. FEE_RECIPIENTS.md lists 8 normal, 8 reserved and 8 buyback recipients.

facts.topic: PumpSwap pricing uses signed effective quote reserves
facts.claim: PumpSwap is constant-product and is priced on effective_quote_reserves = pool_quote_token_account.amount + Pool.virtual_quote_reserves (i128). Since September 30 the virtual field may be negative, but the sum is guaranteed non-negative and to fit in u64. The base side uses the raw vault balance. On 2026-10-06, two sampled canonical SOL pools (9jkXWMyt..., CHtrRatG...) carried virtual_quote_reserves of about +17.58 SOL (17,584,326,063 and 17,584,505,288 lamports), and a non-canonical pool carried 0. That contradicts the older README line saying the value is 0 on all pools today.
facts.design_relevance: A local PumpSwap quoter that ignores this field misprices by about 17.6 SOL of quote depth. The adapter needs a signed i128 decoder and a unit test with a negative value.
facts.note: Both named canonical pools carry vqr 17,584,326,063 and 17,584,505,288. Two freshly migrated pools carry 17,584,172,944 and 17,544,146,214, so the value changes over time. PUMP_SWAP_README still says it is '0 on all pools today', which is stale. The non-negative guarantee is documented. Where the value comes from is now partly explained: an InitBoostEvent sets it at migration (see missed_critical).

It also has the unified buy_v2 (27 accounts), sell_v2 (26) and buy_exact_quote_in_v2 (27), where every account is mandatory. The v2 instructions are required for USDC-paired coins; SOL coins pass the wSOL mint while still settling in native SOL. create_v2 coins use Token-2022. On-chain Global.whitelisted_quote_mints = USDC (EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v) and initial_virtual_quote_reserves = 4,292,000,000 (USDC units). PumpSwap buy (base_amount_out, max_quote_amount_in) and buy_exact_quote_in take 23 accounts; sell takes 21. Official SDKs: @pump-fun/pump-sdk, @pump-fun/pump-swap-sdk and the Rust crate pump-rust-client.
facts.design_relevance: Direct integration is fully specified by the official IDL. Use the v2 instructions so SOL and USDC coins share one code path.
facts.note: Account counts match: buy 16, sell 14, buy_v2 27, sell_v2 26, buy_exact_quote_in_v2 27; PumpSwap buy 23, buy_exact_quote_in 23, sell 21. whitelisted_quote_mints = [USDC] and initial_virtual_quote_reserves = 4,292,000,000 on-chain. facts.claim: The official docs record repeated breaking or semantic changes. (1) A creator-fee upgrade added creator_vault accounts and extended BondingCurve, announced for "Monday, May 12, 11:00 AM UTC". (2) A dynamic market-cap fee structure made 2 new buy/sell accounts mandatory from "Monday, September 1, 20:00 UTC"; the docs advised raising slippage as a mitigation. (3) Unified v2 trade instructions. (4) Holder-rewards coins and cashback deprecation (repo commits on 2026-09-12 and 2026-09-14). (5) Negative virtual quote reserves from September 30 (commit on 2026-09-29). The pages do not state years for (1) and (2).
facts.design_relevance: A direct adapter needs IDL version pinning, a watch on the docs repo and program upgrades, and a canary simulation before each session. Upgrades should trigger an automatic trading halt.
facts.note: The quoted dates and the commits on 2026-09-12, 2026-09-14 and 2026-09-29 are confirmed. The pages give no years, but git history dates them: the creator-fee doc was committed 2025-05-08 (Mon May 12 = 2025), the fee-program README 2025-08-29 (Mon Sep 1 = 2025), and USDC-paired v2 2026-05-07. These are past events.

facts.claim: The PumpSwap GlobalConfig admin can call `disable` to globally disable create_pool, deposit, withdraw, buy or sell. The Pump Global authority can change all Global parameters via set_params. Fee tiers live in FeeConfig accounts that admin instructions (upsert_fee_tiers, update_fee_config) can change. Raydium LaunchLab GlobalConfig fields are updatable via UpdateConfig by the program admin.
facts.design_relevance: Fees and venue availability can change without notice. The bot should subscribe to config accounts, recompute costs on change, and fail closed if a venue is disabled while holding inventory.
facts.note: disable, set_params, upsert_fee_tiers and update_fee_config all exist. Raydium UpdateConfig accepts the LaunchLab program admin or the delegated create-config authority, not the admin only. PumpSwap disable_flags is 0 on-chain.

facts.claim: The pump FAQ recommends a static compute-unit limit of about 100,000 for buy/sell instead of simulating first, because simulation slows submission. Buys that complete the curve use slightly more CU. The official Rust buy_v2 example sets 400,000 CU. buy_v2 initializes user_volume_accumulator (137 bytes) on first use, paid by the user at 0.0018444 SOL rent, and may create ATAs (rent if missing).
facts.design_relevance: Gives per-venue CU budgets for the transaction builder. One-time rent belongs in the bankroll cost model, and ATA closes should be scheduled to reclaim rent.
facts.note: The FAQ recommends a static limit 'like 100_000' and says the completing buy runs more code. The Rust example sets 400_000. BUY.md lists rent of 0.0018444 SOL for the 137-byte account, which matches the rent formula (265 x 6960 lamports), plus ATA rent if missing.

facts.claim: Graduation triggers when quote_vault reaches the launch's own threshold (total_quote_fund_raising). The SOL GlobalConfig 6s1xP3... has min_quote_fund_raising = 24 SOL on-chain (doc default 30e9). New launches must use CPSWAP, and MigrateToCpswap is signed by the migrate_to_cpswap_wallet on GlobalConfig, so it is not permissionless. The post-graduation CPMM AmmConfig comes from PlatformConfig.cpswap_config, not a fixed 0.25% tier. On-chain on 2026-10-06, 128 of 133 'StonkFun' PlatformConfigs bind to CPMM AmmConfig index 3 (4.00% trade fee, 0.05% creator rate). Across all 3,627 PlatformConfigs, index 3 (1,368) is more common than index 0 (1,263; 0.25% + 0.05%). LaunchLab source is not public.
facts.design_relevance: The graduation trigger differs per launch and must be read from PoolState. Migration timing depends on Raydium's crank, unlike pump.fun's permissionless migrate.
facts.original_claim: A LaunchLab launch graduates when quote_vault reaches its per-launch threshold (PoolState.total_quote_fund_raising). The SOL GlobalConfig (6s1xP3hpbAfFoNtUNF8mfHsjr2Bd97JxFJRWLbL6aHuX) has min_quote_fund_raising = 24,000,000,000 lamports (24 SOL) on-chain; the docs' default is 30,000,000,000. New launches must migrate to Raydium CPMM (migrate_type CPSWAP). MigrateToCpswap is signed by the migrate_to_cpswap_wallet stored on GlobalConfig (a Raydium-operated crank), so it is not permissionless. Post-graduation fees follow the CPMM config the pool binds to ('typically AmmConfig[0], the 0.25% tier'). LaunchLab source is not public; its IDL is published in raydium-io/raydium-idl.
facts.note: The overview's 'typically AmmConfig[0], the 0.25% tier' is contradicted by on-chain PlatformConfig.cpswap_config values. platform-config.md defines cpswap_config as 'CPMM AmmConfig that the post-grad pool will bind to'. Graduated StonkFun tokens can therefore carry a 4%+ CPMM fee.

facts.claim: On 2026-10-06 the LaunchLab program held 3,626 PlatformConfig accounts. Many share a display name ('letsbonk.fun', 'StonkFun', 'Raydium') but have different fee_rate and creator_fee_rate. For example, 'letsbonk.fun' configs range from fee_rate 0 to 12,500 and creator_fee_rate 0 to 5,000. Name, web and image are free-form fields stored on the account.
facts.design_relevance: Never infer fees or legitimacy from the platform name. Key the venue config on PlatformConfig pubkey allowlists.
facts.note: I now count 3,627 accounts (one more than the claim). 'letsbonk.fun' has 29 configs with fee_rate 0 to 12,500 and creator 0 to 5,000. The name, web and img fields are free-form inline arrays.

facts.claim: DBC program: dbcij3LWUppWqq96dh6gJWwBifmcGfLSB5D4DuSMaqN. Trading fee = base fee + optional dynamic (volatility) fee, with numerators over 1,000,000,000. The minimum base fee is 0.25% and the total cap is 99%. Base-fee modes: linear or exponential schedulers, which can start high as anti-sniper fees and decay; a rate limiter that is deprecated for new configs; or a fixed fee. Protocol takes 20% of the trading fee, referral gets 20% of the protocol fee, and the rest is split between partner and creator. Fees can be collected in the quote token or the output token.
facts.design_relevance: Early DBC buys can pay extreme scheduled fees (up to 99%). The adapter must compute the current fee from the pool config and timestamp before every quote and refuse entries above a fee ceiling.
facts.note: The program ID, the 1e9 denominator, the 0.25% minimum, the 99% cap, the 20% protocol share, the 20%-of-protocol referral and the quote/output collect modes are confirmed. One nuance: the docs say fixed fee is a product pattern built from a scheduler config, not a separate on-chain mode.

facts.claim: When the quote reserve reaches the configured threshold, DBC curve trading stops and the pool migrates in steps (PreBondingCurve → PostBondingCurve → LockedVesting → CreatedPool). New configs must migrate to DAMM v2; DAMM v1 is deprecated for new pools. A fixed 0.2% protocol liquidity migration fee applies, plus an optional partner/creator migration fee. At least 10% of migrated liquidity must stay locked on day 1, so up to 90% can be unlocked. Vesting locks are capped at 2 years.
facts.design_relevance: Post-graduation DBC tokens can have mostly withdrawable LP. The risk module (TH) should read lock percentages before the bot holds through migration.
facts.note: The state sequence, DAMM v2 being required for new configs, the fixed 0.2% protocol migration fee, the optional partner/creator migration fee, the at least 10% locked at day 1 and the 2-year vesting cap all match.

facts.topic: Meteora DAMM v2 and DLMM fees
facts.claim: DAMM v2 program: cpamdpZCGKUy5JxQXB4dcpGPiikHawvSWAd6mEn1sGG. Total fee = min(base + dynamic, pool cap) over a 1e9 denominator, with a 1 bps minimum and caps up to 99% (version-0 pools 50%). Protocol takes 20% of the trading fee by default. Base modes are a time scheduler and a market-cap scheduler (fee decays as price rises), each linear or exponential. DLMM program: LBUZKhRxPF3XUpBCjp4YzTKgLccjZhTSDM9YuVaPwxo. It is bin-based with bin step up to 400 bps, and charges a base fee plus a variable fee that rises with volatility (bins crossed or rapid swaps).
facts.design_relevance: Meteora fees are pool-specific and time- or volatility-dependent. Prefer aggregator quotes (/build) for these venues over hand-written quoters in phase 1.
facts.note: min(base+dynamic, cap) over 1e9, the 1 bps minimum, the 99% cap (50% for v0 pools), the 20% protocol default and the time/market-cap schedulers (linear or exponential) all match. The DLMM program ID, the 400 bps maximum bin step and the variable fee also match.

facts.topic: Raydium AMM v4, CPMM and CLMM fee tiers
facts.claim: AMM v4 (675kPX...) charges 0.25% (88% LP / 12% protocol) with no creator fee. It still accepts new pools via Initialize2, but the UI, SDK and API default new pools to CPMM. CPMM (CPMMoo8L...) has 21 configs with trade fees from 0.005% to 4.00%, plus an additive creator rate of 0.05% to 1.495% that applies only when the pool enabled the creator fee. Config 0 is 0.25% + 0.05% on-chain, and config 16 is 0.005% + 1.495%. CLMM has 18 configs from 0.01% to 4.00%.

facts.topic: Jupiter swap API products and base URLs
facts.claim: Jupiter Swap API V2 is at https://api.jup.ag/swap/v2. The Meta-Aggregator path, GET /order + POST /execute, has the Metis, JupiterZ (RFQ), DFlow and OKX routers compete. It returns an assembled transaction and lands it through /execute (RTSE slippage, priority-fee strategy, Jupiter Beam pipeline, confirmation polling). The Router path, GET /build, is Metis-only and returns raw instructions plus address lookup tables; the caller lands them via their own RPC or tx.jup.ag. JupiterZ transactions cannot be modified. Ultra (https://ultra-api.jup.ag /order and /execute) moved to the same endpoints at the new base URL. Metis v1 (/swap/v1/quote + /swap/v1/swap-instructions) maps to /swap/v2/build.
facts.design_relevance: Choosing /order (managed landing, fee, no modification) versus /build (no fee, full control, self-landing) is a key decision branch for the execution layer.
facts.note: Everything in the claim is stated in current docs. One extra point: metis-to-build says /build is ExactIn only (swapMode is not supported).

facts.claim: Jupiter charges a platform fee on /order swaps: 0 bps for buying Jupiter tokens and for pegged pairs, 2 bps SOL-stable, 5 bps LST-stable, 10 bps for everything else, and 50 bps for 'New tokens (within 24 hours of token age)'. Gasless support can add further bps to the top-level feeBps. Jupiter charges no swap fee on /build; the only fee there is an optional integrator platformFeeBps.
facts.design_relevance: On fresh meme tokens /order can add 0.5% per side on top of the pump fees, which makes /build or direct program calls materially cheaper.
facts.note: The fee table (0/0/2/5/10/50 for new tokens under 24h), gasless additions to top-level feeBps and 'Jupiter does not charge swap fees on /build' all match.

facts.topic: Observed Jupiter fee and routability on brand-new pump tokens

facts.topic: Jupiter routing eligibility for new markets
facts.claim: Metis 'instant routing' auto-lists new markets on eligible DEXes during a grace period based on token age, not market age. Eligible DEXes include Pump.fun, Pump.fun AMM, Raydium LaunchLab, Raydium CPMM and CLMM, Meteora DBC, Dynamic AMM, DAMM V2 and DLMM, Whirlpool, Moonshot, Virtuals, Boop.fun and Fluxbeam. A bonding curve that does not graduate before the grace period ends is removed; the graduated market is added. After the grace period, markets are re-checked every 30 minutes. They must show a $500 round-trip loss under 30% or a $1,000-vs-$500 price-impact gap under 20%. When Metis drops a market, /build returns 'No routes found' while /order may still route via another router.
facts.design_relevance: Jupiter-only exits can disappear for illiquid tokens. A direct program-level sell path is a needed fallback so the bot is never stuck holding a position.
facts.note: Grace period by token age, curve removal and graduated-market addition, the 30-minute recheck, the $500 under 30% and $1000-vs-$500 under 20% criteria, and /build 'No routes found' while /order may still route all match. The eligible list also includes plain 'Raydium' and 'Meteora Dynamic AMM'.

facts.claim: tx.jup.ag is a send-only, Solana-RPC-compatible sendTransaction endpoint. It requires a Jupiter API key and a Jupiter tip of at least 1,000,000 lamports (0.001 SOL) to one of 16 tip accounts per transaction. Tipping more does not improve landing. A success response means 'accepted and forwarded, not that it landed'. It accepts any signed transaction, not only Jupiter swaps. /build's tipAmount parameter adds the tip instruction automatically.
facts.design_relevance: A 0.001 SOL flat tip is about 1% of a 0.1 SOL trade. For small positions it can exceed the venue fee, so the cost model must include it (landing details are owned by LD).
facts.note: Send-only, API key required, minimum 0.001 SOL tip to one of 16 accounts, 'tipping more does not improve landing', accepted is not landed, any signed tx, and tipAmount on /build all match. Default routing is SWQoS + Jito, and Beam adds a small Jito tip.

facts.claim: /build requires inputMint, outputMint, amount and taker. Options include: slippageBps as a number or 'rtse'; mode=fast (BETA: Bellman-Ford with no route splitting, priority-fee lookup in parallel, possibly worse pricing); maxAccounts (default 64, range 1–64); dexes and excludeDexes (case-sensitive labels); platformFeeBps with feeAccount; payer; forJitoBundle; tipAmount; computeUnitPricePercentile. The docs advise validating and capping the returned compute-unit price before signing.
facts.design_relevance: Using dexes=[Pump.fun, Pump.fun Amm], mode=fast and a CU-price clamp gives a fee-free, fast fallback quote and build path.
facts.note: The required and optional parameters, fast mode (BETA, Bellman-Ford without splitting, parallel priority-fee lookup) and the advice to validate and cap CU price all match. /build is ExactIn only.

facts.claim: Metis, Jupiter's on-chain router, is offered as a self-hosted API binary at metis.builders. It needs a Binary Key, which requires at least 10,000 JUP staked at vote.jup.ag, one key per binary instance, and your own RPC (Yellowstone gRPC recommended; RPC polling mode also supported).

facts.note: At least 10,000 JUP staked at vote.jup.ag, one key per binary instance, your own RPC required, Yellowstone gRPC recommended and a poll mode supported all match.

facts.topic: pump.fun migration puts ~17.58 SOL into virtual, not real, PumpSwap quote reserves (boost)

facts.claim: getTransaction on recent pump and withdraw-authority transactions returned error -32015 'Transaction version (1) is not supported by the requesting client' unless maxSupportedTransactionVersion was 1. With version 1 the same calls succeed.
facts.design_relevance: Reconciliation and event decoders that request version 0 will silently miss a share of fills and migrations, which would corrupt after-cost P&L.

facts.topic: Meteora DBC auto-migration depends on keeper thresholds
facts.claim: Meteora's two mainnet migration keepers auto-migrate completed DBC pools only when the quote threshold matches listed quote mints and minimums (for example 10 SOL or 750 USDC), or meets the Jupiter-verified quote conditions. Other pools need a manual migration.
facts.design_relevance: Graduation-to-tradeable-pool latency on DBC is not guaranteed. A position can be stuck in a completed curve where curve trading has stopped until someone migrates it.

facts.topic: pump.fun curves can complete in the creation transaction
facts.claim: For mint REDeUNrb..., a single transaction emitted CreateEvent, TradeEvent and CompleteEvent, and migration followed in the same slot (453916006).
facts.design_relevance: A graduation detector and curve-entry strategy must handle coins that never had a tradeable curve phase. The first tradeable venue for such coins is the PumpSwap pool.

facts.claim: The base fee is 5,000 lamports per signature, including signatures checked by the Ed25519, Secp256k1 and Secp256r1 precompiles. 50% of the base fee is burned and 50% goes to the block-producing validator. The prioritization fee goes 100% to the validator under SIMD-0096. The whole fee is deducted from the fee payer before execution and is charged even if the transaction fails.
facts.design_relevance: A failed swap still costs base fee plus priority fee. The cost model and paper-trading simulator must charge fees on failed attempts as well as on fills.
facts.note: The doc states 5,000 lamports per signature, including Ed25519, Secp256k1 and Secp256r1 precompile signatures. The base fee is split 50% burned and 50% to the validator, and 100% of the priority fee goes to the validator (SIMD-0096). The fee is deducted before execution and charged on failure. It cites agave v3.1.8.

facts.claim: For legacy and v0 transactions: prioritization_fee = ceil(compute_unit_price [micro-lamports per CU] x compute_unit_limit / 1,000,000) lamports. The fee uses the REQUESTED CU limit, not the CUs actually used. The default CU price is 0. With no SetComputeUnitLimit instruction, the default limit is 200,000 CU per non-builtin instruction and 3,000 CU per builtin instruction, capped at 1,400,000 CU per transaction. The docs recommend simulating and adding a 10% margin. The block limit is 60,000,000 CU and the per-writable-account limit is 12,000,000 CU. Helius's priority-fee page instead says fee = price x CUs 'consumed', which conflicts with the Solana docs; the Solana docs are authoritative.
facts.design_relevance: Over-requesting CUs wastes money. The tx builder must simulate, then set the CU limit to the measured value plus about 10% before pricing the fee.
facts.note: Every element checks out: the formula ceil(price x limit / 1e6), pricing on the requested limit, default price 0, defaults of 200k per non-builtin and 3k per builtin instruction, the 1.4M cap, simulate plus 10%, and the 60M block and 12M writable-account limits. The Helius page does say 'Price per compute unit x Compute units consumed', which conflicts with the Solana docs.

facts.claim: The Compute Budget Program (ComputeBudget111111111111111111111111111111) has 4 instructions: RequestHeapFrame (discriminator 1, u32 bytes, 32 KiB-256 KiB, multiple of 1,024), SetComputeUnitLimit (2, u32), SetComputeUnitPrice (3, u64 micro-lamports) and SetLoadedAccountsDataSizeLimit (4, u32, nonzero, clamped to 64 MiB). Only one of each type is allowed; a duplicate fails the whole transaction with DuplicateInstruction. Each ComputeBudget instruction costs 150 CU and one instruction slot.
facts.design_relevance: The tx-builder ticket must dedupe compute-budget instructions, since aggregator-supplied instructions may already contain them and a duplicate fails the transaction.
facts.note: The docs list the four variants with discriminators 1-4 and the stated parameter types. Heap must be 32-256 KiB and a multiple of 1,024. The data-size limit must be nonzero and is clamped to 64 MiB. A duplicate fails with DuplicateInstruction. The versioned-tx doc says each ComputeBudget instruction costs an instruction slot and 150 CU.

facts.claim: The txv1 feature gate (txv1aq4pp281K9um3tnPgkfX8UqtFT6wcVW3hNezGLL) activated on mainnet at the start of epoch 1035 on 2026-09-15 at about 01:00 UTC (SIMD-0296 / SIMD-0385). v1 transactions: max 4,096 bytes; up to 64 inline addresses and NO address lookup tables; the priority fee is an absolute lamport total in the message config; the CU limit and loaded-accounts-data-size limit default to 0 and must be set explicitly or the transaction fails; ComputeBudget instructions run as 150-CU no-ops; sends over 1,232 bytes require base64 encoding. Legacy and v0 transactions keep working unchanged.
facts.design_relevance: Sending v1 is opt-in. The bot can stay on v0, which keeps ALT-based aggregator routes and ComputeBudget pricing, but it must still handle READING v1 transactions (see LD-05).
facts.note: The page matches on all points: gate txv1aq4pp281K9um3tnPgkfX8UqtFT6wcVW3hNezGLL, epoch 1035 on 2026-09-15 at about 01:00 UTC, SIMD-0296/0385, 4,096 bytes, 64 inline addresses, no ALTs, and the priority fee as a lamport total. CU and data-size limits default to 0, ComputeBudget instructions run as 150-CU no-ops, base64 is needed above 1,232 bytes, and legacy/v0 are unchanged. The page says 'Updated September 2026'.

facts.topic: Transaction format v1 - breaking changes for readers, libraries and Jito leaders
facts.claim: getTransaction and getBlock need maxSupportedTransactionVersion set to the integer 1; the value 0 or an omitted parameter fails. getTransaction on a v1 transaction returns error -32015, and a single v1 transaction fails an entire getBlock response. blockSubscribe emits block: null and stops advancing. Geyser/gRPC consumers with old protobufs silently misread v1 as v0 with a zeroed compute budget. Fee analytics that scan ComputeBudget instructions report zero for v1. Minimum versions with v1 support: @solana/kit 8.0.0; @solana/web3.js 3.x (1.99.0 can read v1 but cannot build or send it); solana-* Rust crates 4.2.x; solders 0.29.0; yellowstone-grpc-proto 12.6.0; Yellowstone geyser plugin 15.1.1; @triton-one/yellowstone-grpc 6.0.0. Jito-Solana validators before v4.2.2 will not build v1 transactions into blocks. RPC nodes before Agave v4.2.2 downgrade v1 to v0 in storage.
facts.design_relevance: Ingestion, fill-reconciliation and fee-analytics tickets must opt in to v1 and use v1-aware decoders. Otherwise the bot can silently stall or misreport fees when market participants send v1 transactions.
facts.note: Every reader-breakage item and minimum version matches the page. Precise details: web3.js 3.x support starts at 3.0.0-rc.3, and Geyser plugins before 15.1.1 downgrade v1 to v0 before it reaches the wire. The page itself lists yellowstone-grpc-client 'Latest is 13.3.0', which is stale (crates.io shows 14.0.1).

facts.topic: Size, accounts and address lookup tables
facts.claim: Legacy and v0 transactions are capped at 1,232 bytes, and the runtime enforces 64 accounts per transaction (128 behind an inactive feature). A v0 transaction can reference address lookup tables. Each ALT stores up to 256 addresses. ALT entries cannot be signers, and an address cannot be looked up in the same slot it was added. The base58 encoding for sendTransaction stays capped at 1,232 bytes.
facts.design_relevance: Use base64 everywhere. Multi-hop swaps need v0 plus ALTs. Jito says tip accounts must not be placed in an ALT (LD-19).
facts.note: Confirmed: 1,232 bytes, 64 accounts (128 behind an inactive increase_tx_account_lock_limit), up to 256 keys per ALT, ALT entries cannot be signers, no lookup in the slot the address was added, and base58 capped at 1,232 bytes.

facts.claim: A recent blockhash is valid for 150 slots (MAX_PROCESSING_AGE), and the BlockhashQueue holds 300 entries. Solana production guidance: fetch the blockhash at 'confirmed' commitment, store lastValidBlockHeight, send with maxRetries: 0 and handle retries yourself, rebroadcast the same signed transaction (same signature, idempotent), and rebuild with a fresh blockhash only after BLOCK_HEIGHT_EXCEEDED / BLOCKHASH_NOT_FOUND. skipPreflight: true trades away validation for latency.
facts.design_relevance: Order-execution state machine: rebroadcast the same signed tx until lastValidBlockHeight passes. Re-sign only after expiry is confirmed, or a buy can execute twice.
facts.note: Confirmed: MAX_PROCESSING_AGE is 150 slots and MAX_RECENT_BLOCKHASHES is 300. The production doc says to fetch the blockhash at confirmed, store lastValidBlockHeight, send with maxRetries 0, treat resubmission of the same signed tx as idempotent, rebuild on BLOCK_HEIGHT_EXCEEDED or BLOCKHASH_NOT_FOUND, and that skipPreflight trades validation for latency.

facts.topic: Slot time / blockhash window in wall-clock terms
facts.claim: Under SIMD-0525, mainnet slot time targets went 400 to 350 ms (2026-08-21, epoch 1020), 300 ms (2026-08-28, epoch 1024) and 250 ms (2026-09-18, epoch 1037). 200 ms is scheduled for epoch 1052 (slot 454,464,000). The Solana Foundation says blockhash expiry is about 50 s at 250 ms and about 40 s at 200 ms, and an epoch of 432,000 slots lasts about 30 h at 250 ms. Observed on 2026-10-06 via public RPC: 6,766 slots in 1,800 s across 30 getRecentPerformanceSamples ending at slot 453,898,859, about 266 ms per slot; getBlockTime across slots 453,798,992 to 453,898,992 gives 26,701 s per 100,000 slots, about 267 ms per slot. The core Transactions/production docs still say '~60-90 seconds', which is stale.
facts.design_relevance: Never hardcode 400 ms or a 60-90 s expiry. Derive timeouts from block height and the measured slot duration, and expect about 40 s windows within days.
facts.note: The page ('Updated October 2026') matches all dates, epochs and slots: 350 ms at epoch 1020, 300 ms at 1024, 250 ms at 1037, and 200 ms scheduled at epoch 1052 (slot 454,464,000). It gives about 50 s expiry at 250 ms, about 40 s at 200 ms, and about 30 h per epoch. I re-ran getBlockTime: 26,701 s per 100k slots, about 267 ms per slot. A fresh 30-sample read gave 6,725 slots in 1,800 s (about 268 ms). The production doc still says about 60-90 s.

facts.claim: Commitment levels: 'processed' is the newest slot on the node's best fork and can be rolled back; 'confirmed' means at least two-thirds of active stake voted; 'finalized' means maximum vote lockout. In sendTransaction, preflightCommitment defaults to finalized. When skipPreflight is true, preflightCommitment is ignored and the node uses processed internally. If maxRetries is unset, the RPC node retries until finalized or until the blockhash expires. A success response only means the node accepted the transaction, not that it landed; use getSignatureStatuses.
facts.design_relevance: The dashboard and the risk engine must treat 'sent' and 'landed/confirmed' as different states. Position state should update on 'confirmed', with a finalized reconciliation pass afterwards.
facts.note: The commitment definitions match. preflightCommitment defaults to finalized and is ignored under skipPreflight (the node uses processed). With maxRetries unset, the node retries until finalized or the blockhash expires. A success response does not guarantee the tx was processed; use getSignatureStatuses.

facts.claim: A durable-nonce transaction puts AdvanceNonceAccount as instruction 0 and uses the stored nonce in place of the recent blockhash, which removes the 150-slot expiry. Solana docs warn that durable nonces 'may be deprecated in a future release' (SIMD discussion 415). Nozomi's docs say block builders may deprioritize durable-nonce transactions as spam-associated (vendor statement).
facts.design_relevance: Do not use durable nonces for routine trading. Expiring blockhashes give natural staleness protection for time-sensitive orders.
facts.note: AdvanceNonceAccount must be instruction 0 and the nonce replaces the blockhash. The 'may be deprecated' warning links SIMD discussion 415. Nozomi says block builders may deprioritize durable-nonce txs as spam-associated (vendor statement).

facts.claim: getRecentPrioritizationFees takes an optional array of up to 128 writable-account addresses and returns per-slot prioritizationFee values in micro-lamports per CU. The node cache covers up to 150 blocks. Triton's docs say the standard method returns the MINIMUM fee paid per slot, often zero. Observed on 2026-10-06: an unfiltered call to the public mainnet RPC returned 150 slots (453,898,666 to 453,898,815) and all 150 had prioritizationFee = 0.
facts.design_relevance: Unfiltered native output is useless for pricing. Use account-filtered queries on the pool or mint accounts the swap writes, or a percentile estimator (LD-12).
facts.note: Confirmed: max 128 addresses, fees in micro-lamports per CU, cache of up to 150 blocks, and Triton's statement that the method returns the minimum fee. My own unfiltered call returned 150 slots (453,910,587-453,910,736), all with prioritizationFee 0.

facts.topic: Priority fee estimation - provider APIs (verified names)
facts.claim: Helius getPriorityFeeEstimate (1 credit) returns levels Min, Low (25th percentile), Medium (50th), High (75th), VeryHigh (95th) and UnsafeMax, from a serialized transaction or account keys. QuickNode qn_estimatePriorityFees requires the 'Solana Priority Fee API' add-on; last_n_blocks has a maximum and default of 100; it returns percentiles and the tiers low (25), medium (50), high (75), extreme (90), both per CU and per transaction. Triton adds a 'percentile' parameter (1-10,000) to getRecentPrioritizationFees.
facts.design_relevance: The fee-oracle ticket can use a provider estimator behind an interface, with a hard per-trade fee cap set as a % of notional.
facts.note: Helius getPriorityFeeEstimate has the levels Min/Low25/Medium50/High75/VeryHigh95/UnsafeMax and costs 1 credit. QuickNode needs the add-on; last_n_blocks has max and default 100; it returns low/medium/high/extreme at 25/50/75/90, per CU and per transaction, plus a 'recommended' field. Triton's percentile parameter takes 1-10,000.

facts.claim: min_balance = (128 + data_size) x lamports_per_byte. SIMD-0437 cuts lamports_per_byte from 6,960 to 696 in 5 feature-gated steps; step 1 (6,333) went live 2026-09-03 at epoch 1028. Observed on mainnet on 2026-10-06: getMinimumBalanceForRentExemption(165) = 1,488,440 lamports (0.00148844 SOL), (170) = 1,513,840, and (0) = 650,240. That implies 5,080 lamports per byte, so step 2 is live. The Foundation page still marks step 2 'Live on Testnet', which is stale versus the chain. Steps 3-5 (2,575 / 1,322 / 696) are 'expected in Agave 4.4 (November 2026)', and a fallback gate can reset the value to 6,960.
facts.design_relevance: Never hardcode 2,039,280 lamports. Query getMinimumBalanceForRentExemption at startup and each epoch, because the value will change again.
facts.note: My re-run returned 1,488,440 (165 bytes), 1,513,840 (170) and 650,240 (0), which is 5,080 lamports per byte, so step 2 is live on mainnet. The page still marks step 2 'Live on Testnet'. Steps 3-5 are 'Expected in Agave 4.4' (November 2026). A fallback gate exists to reset to 6,960.

facts.topic: Rent - refundability and Token-2022 account size
facts.claim: Rent is a fully refundable deposit: closing an account returns its lamports in full to whoever closes it. An SPL Token account is 165 bytes. Associated Token Accounts under Token-2022 always include the ImmutableOwner extension. From the token-2022 source code: base length 165 bytes, plus 1 byte AccountType, plus a 4-byte TLV header (u16 type + u16 length), plus a zero-size ImmutableOwner struct, gives 170 bytes, currently 1,513,840 lamports. Other account extensions, such as TransferFeeAmount, add bytes.
facts.design_relevance: Each new token position locks about 0.0015 SOL of refundable rent. Close token accounts after a full exit and show locked rent separately from P&L on the dashboard. The 170-byte size is derived from source, not observed on chain.
facts.note: Rent is a 'fully refundable bond'. The ATA program 'always uses' ImmutableOwner, which is a zero-size struct. BASE_ACCOUNT_AND_TYPE_LENGTH is 165+1, plus a u16 type and u16 length TLV header, giving 170 bytes; rent for 170 bytes is 1,513,840 on chain now. I could not observe an actual ATA on chain either: the public RPC returned 429 on getTokenLargestAccounts in my session too.

facts.claim: The Solana docs say transactions go directly to upcoming leaders rather than a shared mempool, unprocessed transactions expire after about 150 blocks ('~1 minute', now stale given 250 ms slots), and sandwiching still occurs via bundles like [frontrun_tx, your_tx, backrun_tx]. arXiv:2609.28115 is an unrefereed preprint, not peer-reviewed: 'No Place to Hide: An Analysis on Protected Order Flow Sandwich Attacks', by Heimbach, Solmaz, Öz and Ferreira Torres, submitted 2026-09-23. It is a three-year, six-chain study that identifies 28.0 million sandwich attacks on Solana against transactions intended to be protected from front-running, finds that such attacks rarely occur tightly around their victims, and reports validator- and application-level exposure on Solana.
facts.design_relevance: There is no public mempool, but ordinary swaps are still sandwichable. Strict minAmountOut and slippage limits are mandatory, and 'protected' routing reduces but does not remove exposure.
facts.original_claim: The Solana docs state that transactions are forwarded directly to upcoming leaders, not held in a shared mempool, and that unprocessed transactions expire after about 150 blocks. They also state that sandwiching still occurs, e.g. via bundles of the form [frontrun_tx, your_tx, backrun_tx]. A peer-reviewable measurement study (arXiv:2609.28115, Heimbach, Solmaz, Öz, Ferreira Torres, v1 2026-09-23) identifies 28.0 million sandwich attacks on Solana against transactions intended to be protected from front-running over a three-year window. It finds that these attacks rarely sit tightly around their victims and that Solana has validator- and application-level exposure.
facts.note: The numbers and authors are right. It must be labelled an arXiv preprint (v1), not peer-reviewed or peer-reviewable evidence.

facts.claim: Add any valid pubkey starting with 'jitodontfront' (marked read-only, need not exist on chain) to any instruction. The Jito block engine then rejects any bundle containing that transaction unless the transaction is at index 0. This works with sendTransaction and sendBundle and supports ALTs. Jito's disclaimer: it may reduce sandwiching, is not guaranteed, and applies only to the Jito block engine.
facts.design_relevance: This is a free protection. Add a dontfront account to every swap the bot sends, but log it as a mitigation, not a guarantee.
facts.note: Any valid pubkey with the jitodontfront prefix can be added to any instruction. Read-only is recommended and the account need not exist. Bundles are rejected unless that tx is at index 0. Works with sendTransaction and sendBundle and supports ALTs. The disclaimer matches. The page says 'Last updated on Sep 09, 2026'.

facts.claim: A bundle holds at most 5 transactions, executed sequentially and atomically within one slot. The minimum tip is 1,000 lamports. A tip is any SOL transfer, top-level or CPI, to one of 8 tip accounts returned by getTipAccounts; pick one at random. getTipAccounts on 2026-10-06 returned the same 8 accounts listed in the docs. Jito says not to use ALTs for tip accounts, and that tips are wasted when the leader is not running Jito-Solana. The Jito sendTransaction proxy always sets skip_preflight=true, and bundleOnly=true gives revert protection. For sendTransaction Jito recommends splitting spend about 70% priority fee / 30% tip; for sendBundle only the tip matters.
facts.design_relevance: Put the tip inside the swap transaction so a failed swap pays no tip, and route Jito tips only when the upcoming leader runs a Jito-family client.
facts.note: Confirmed: up to 5 txs executed sequentially and atomically, 1,000-lamport minimum tip, any top-level or CPI transfer to one of 8 tip accounts picked at random, no ALTs for tip accounts, and tips wasted on non-Jito leaders. sendTransaction always uses skip_preflight=true, and bundleOnly=true gives revert protection. The split is 70/30 for sendTransaction; only the tip matters for sendBundle. My getTipAccounts call returned the same 8 accounts as the docs.

facts.topic: Jito block-engine endpoints, rate limits, uncle risk
facts.claim: Mainnet block engines: global https://mainnet.block-engine.jito.wtf plus regional amsterdam, dublin, frankfurt, london, ny, slc, singapore and tokyo .mainnet.block-engine.jito.wtf. The default rate limit is 1 request per second per IP per region with no auth key required; exceeding it returns 429. Jito warns that bundle transactions landing in uncled (skipped) blocks can be rebroadcast and land outside bundle atomicity. Its advice is to keep the tip in the same transaction as the core logic, with pre/post state checks.
facts.design_relevance: Keyless Jito access limits the bot to about 1 send per second per region, which suits a low-frequency bot. Each swap must be safe to execute on its own (minAmountOut).
facts.note: The global endpoint plus 8 regional endpoints are listed: amsterdam, dublin, frankfurt, london, ny, slc, singapore and tokyo. The default limit is 1 request/s per IP per region, no auth key is needed, and excess returns 429. The uncled-block rebroadcast warning and the advice to keep the tip in the main tx with pre/post checks are both present.

facts.claim: Stake share computed from public-RPC getClusterNodes clientId (self-reported in gossip) joined with getVoteAccounts activated stake, 2026-10-06 ~12:07 UTC (441.7M SOL across 685 node identities): AgaveBam 36.01%, JitoLabs 27.75%, HarmonicAgave 18.56%, HarmonicFiredancer 6.76%, Firedancer 6.67%, FireBAM 1.70%, Agave 1.12%, Rakurai 0.87%, Frankendancer 0.35%, others <0.3%. facts.claim: Harmonic is an alternative Solana block-building system (clients Salsa for Agave and Samba for Firedancer). Harmonic tips are compute-unit priority fees, 100% to the validator with no tip account. Bundle submission requires whitelisting of the searcher pubkey and uses Jito-compatible protos. Harmonic's FAQ says to embed a dontfront/jitodontfront account for front-running protection, while its bundles page lists jitodontfront support as 'upcoming'. Harmonic states that Jito tip accounts take a 6% protocol fee (a competitor statement).
facts.design_relevance: On Harmonic leaders, priority fee (not Jito tip) is the lever, which is another reason to set a sane priority fee on every transaction.
facts.note: The FAQ says tips are CU priority fees with 100% to the validator and no protocol fee. Bundles need a whitelisted searcher pubkey and use Jito-compatible protos. The FAQ says to embed dontfront/jitodontfront, while the bundles page lists jitodontfront under 'Upcoming features', so the conflict is real. The Jito 6% fee claim is Harmonic's. Extra detail: Harmonic's bundle-control-accounts page says to attach the control account as the FIRST account of a Compute Budget instruction.

facts.claim: Helius Sender consumes no credits, is available on all plans including Free, and is paid by a SOL tip per transaction. Sender Max has a 0.001 SOL minimum tip and routes across Helius, Jito, Harmonic, Rakurai and others (transactions and bundles). SWQOS-only (?swqos_only=true) has a 0.000005 SOL minimum tip and uses a single SWQoS path. Tips between 0.000005 and 0.001 SOL get best-effort routing. Every transaction MUST include a tip transfer to a Helius tip account AND a SetComputeUnitPrice instruction, or it is rejected. Rate limits: 50 req/s per API key per region; keyless 1 req/s per egress IP per region. Regional HTTP endpoints: slc, ewr, lon, fra, ams, sg, tyo. Ping endpoint advised for gaps over 5 s. An opt-in mev-protect=true parameter avoids validators statistically linked to sandwiches; it works on sendTransaction, sendBundle, Sender Max and SWQOS-only.
facts.design_relevance: SWQOS-only with mev-protect is a near-zero fixed-cost landing path. The 0.001 SOL Sender Max floor is about 1% of a 0.1 SOL trade per leg.
facts.note: Every element matches: 0 credits on all plans; Sender Max 0.001 SOL across Helius, Jito, Harmonic and Rakurai; SWQOS-only 0.000005 SOL on a single path; tips in between are best-effort. A tip plus SetComputeUnitPrice is mandatory or the tx is rejected. Limits are 50/s per key per region and 1/s keyless per egress IP per region. Regions are slc, ewr, lon, fra, ams, sg and tyo; ping is advised for gaps over 5 s. mev-protect=true works on all four methods.

facts.claim: Default minimum tip is 0.001 SOL, sent to one of 17 public tip addresses (rotate per transaction). Transactions below the minimum are silently dropped. The tip is an instruction, so it is not paid if the transaction fails. New API keys get 5 req/s per key per region. Nozomi auto-retries until the transaction is confirmed or expires, and client resubmission lowers priority. Default keys are NOT sandwich-protected; an MEV Protect key is available on request and is slower with a higher expiry chance. Signup is self-serve with an API key, and JSON-RPC sendTransaction requires base64. Nozomi says it accepts v1 transactions.
facts.design_relevance: This is an alternative path with a 0.001 SOL floor. Do not layer client retries on top of its built-in retries.
facts.note: Confirmed: 0.001 SOL default minimum, 17 public tip addresses rotated per tx, below-minimum txs silently dropped, tip charged only on landing, 5 req/s per key per region, server-side retries with client resubmission lowering priority, default keys not sandwich-protected, an MEV Protect key on request that is slower with higher expiry risk, self-serve signup, base64 required, and v1 accepted.

facts.claim: Submission requires a system transfer of at least 0.001 SOL to a bloXroute tipping wallet. Modes: useStakedRPCs (fastest; cannot be combined with protection flags); frontRunningProtection with submitProtection SP_LOW (1-slot safety window), SP_MEDIUM (3-slot, the default) or SP_HIGH (8-slot); and revertProtection, which routes only through block engines. The service auto-retries until landed or expired. submit-batch takes up to 25 transactions. Rate limits: Introductory tier 60 credits per 60 s, 1 credit per submit; 'Build Your Own' is 60 + 150 x X credits for $250/month x X.
facts.design_relevance: bloXroute's protection flags add latency by design. Its paid capacity tiers ($250/month increments) are outside the budget.
facts.note: Confirmed: 0.001 SOL minimum tip. useStakedRPCs cannot be combined with frontRunningProtection or revertProtection. SP_LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH are 1/3/8-slot windows with MEDIUM the default. revertProtection routes only through block engines. Auto-retry, batches of up to 25, Introductory at 60 credits per 60 s, 1 credit per submit, and Build Your Own at 60 + 150X for $250X per month.

facts.claim: Documented limits for https://api.mainnet.solana.com: 100 requests per 10 s per IP; 40 requests per 10 s per IP for a single RPC method; 40 concurrent connections; 40 new connections per 10 s; 100 MB per 30 s. facts.design_relevance: Use the public RPC only as a tertiary health-check or fallback reader, never for sending or streaming.

facts.topic: Helius WebSocket connection and subscription caps per plan
facts.claim: Helius LaserStream WebSocket limits: Free allows 5 concurrent connections, Developer 150, Business 250 and Professional 1,000, with 1,000 subscriptions per connection on every plan. Free gets Standard WebSocket types only; Developer and above also get Enhanced. Parsed Streams allow 5 (Free) or 10 (Developer) connections, with 25 subscriptions per connection. All WebSocket data is metered at 2 credits per 0.1 MB uncompressed.
facts.design_relevance: The researcher listed this as unverified. The ingestion design has to fit token and pool subscriptions within 5 connections on Free, and has to budget subscription data against the 1M-credit Free allowance.

facts.topic: Harmonic dontfront placement differs from Jito
facts.claim: Harmonic's Bundle Control Accounts page says to attach the control account ('dontfront' or 'jitodontfront' prefix) as the FIRST account of a Compute Budget instruction. Jito accepts it on any instruction. Harmonic also defines 'dontbund1e', which requires the protected tx at index 0 and lets the other bundle txs invoke only System, Compute Budget and Memo programs. Harmonic's bundles page still lists jitodontfront support as 'upcoming'.
facts.design_relevance: About 25% of stake runs Harmonic clients. Under Harmonic's own docs, a tx that adds jitodontfront only to the swap instruction may not be protected on Harmonic leaders, so the tx-builder ticket must specify where to place the account.

facts.topic: Token-2022 required account extensions change ATA size and swap behaviour
facts.claim: In the token-2022 source, a mint's extensions force matching extensions on every token account: TransferFeeConfig requires TransferFeeAmount, TransferHook requires TransferHookAccount, Pausable requires PausableAccount, and NonTransferable requires NonTransferableAccount plus ImmutableOwner. So a Token-2022 ATA exceeds 170 bytes for such mints, and its rent depends on the mint.
facts.design_relevance: Rent must be computed per mint rather than assumed to be 170 bytes. Transfer-fee, hook or pausable mints change the real cost and exit risk, so the risk engine should detect mint extensions before buying.

facts.topic: Helius webhook delivery can lose events
facts.claim: Helius retries a failed webhook delivery up to 3 times with a 1-second gap. If all attempts fail, the event is permanently lost, with no re-queue. Enhanced webhooks do not send failed transactions; raw webhooks include both successful and failed ones. Each event costs 1 credit even if delivery fails.
facts.design_relevance: Fill reconciliation and position state cannot rely on webhooks alone. The design needs a polling or signature-status reconciliation pass to recover dropped events.

facts.claim: On Chainstack global nodes, a subscribe request may have up to 5 accounts filters and 20 transactions filters, each pubkey list holds up to 200 keys, and filters without conditions are rejected. The SPL Token Program (TokenkegQfeZyiNwAJbNbGKPFXCWuBvf9Ss623VQ5DA) is rejected in accounts.account and in transactions/blocks account_include.
facts.design_relevance: A meme-coin discovery stream cannot just subscribe to all SPL Token activity on this provider. It must filter by launchpad or AMM program IDs, which affects the ingestion ticket and the provider choice.

facts.topic: Helius Sender regional endpoints are plain HTTP
facts.claim: Helius documents its regional server-to-server Sender and ping endpoints as http:// URLs (slc, ewr, lon, fra, ams, sg and tyo, under -sender.helius-rpc.com). Only the global sender.helius-rpc.com endpoint is shown as HTTPS. Keyless /fast requests are limited to 1 request/s per egress IP per region, and rejected 429s count toward that limit.
facts.design_relevance: Signed transactions sent to a regional endpoint travel unencrypted, so on-path observers can see them before they land. If an API key is appended, it is exposed too. The send-path ticket must choose between the HTTPS global endpoint and HTTP regional ones, and must never put a key on plain-HTTP URLs in logs.

facts.topic: Cherry Servers VPS prices (major validator host)
facts.claim: Prices embedded in the Cherry Servers virtual-server pricing page give monthly shared VPS plans at €3 ($3.51) for b2-1-1gb-20s-shared, €6 ($7.02) for b2-2-2gb-40s-shared and €9 ($10.53) for b2-4-4gb-80s-shared. b1 shared plans run €9-€39. The page lists Frankfurt, Amsterdam, Lithuania, Stockholm, Chicago, Singapore and Tokyo. Per-plan availability by location was NOT verified.

facts.topic: Nozomi priority depends on landing history; limits are per region
facts.claim: Nozomi prioritizes by tip and by historical success and landing rates, and a high failure rate lowers priority. Rate limits are per key, per region, per second, so sending the same tx to several regions multiplies effective throughput. Nozomi does not simulate. Its docs advise starting with 100% of the bid in the tip, because a priority fee helps only on non-block-builder paths.
facts.design_relevance: The router and fee policy must pre-check state to avoid sending txs likely to fail, since failures degrade future landing. Fee and tip split rules differ by service: Jito 70/30, Harmonic priority fee only, Nozomi tip-first.

facts.claim: PumpPortal's data WebSocket is wss://pumpportal.fun/api/data?api-key=<key>. subscribeNewToken (token creation) and subscribeMigration are free. subscribeTokenTrade and subscribeAccountTrade are metered at 0.01 SOL per 10,000 messages, and need a PumpPortal API key plus a linked wallet funded with at least 0.02 SOL. Unsubscribe methods are also documented (unsubscribeNewToken/TokenTrade/AccountTrade).
facts.design_relevance: New-token and migration discovery costs nothing. Per-token trade streaming is billed per message, so the watched-token set must be capped and the spend metered.
facts.note: The page gives wss://pumpportal.fun/api/data?api-key=..., lists subscribeNewToken and subscribeMigration as free, and lists subscribeTokenTrade and subscribeAccountTrade at 0.01 SOL per 10000 events (also described as per 10,000 websocket messages). Token or account subscriptions need an API key plus a linked wallet funded with at least 0.02 SOL. It documents unsubscribeNewToken, unsubscribeTokenTrade and unsubscribeAccountTrade, and no unsubscribeMigration.

facts.claim: The PumpPortal FAQ says to use one WebSocket connection and send no more than 200 subscription messages per second, with at most 5,000 addresses per subscribe message. Repeat violations bring temporary bans that expire hourly. Trading and other endpoints are limited to 25 requests/second. The docs warn against opening a new connection per token.
facts.design_relevance: The ingestion service needs a single multiplexed connection, a subscription rate limiter and a ban-aware backoff. Any connection-per-token code must be rejected.
facts.note: The FAQ says: trading and other endpoints are limited to 25 req/s; use one websocket; no more than 200 subscription messages per second; no more than 5000 addresses per message; repeated violations bring temporary bans, and bans expire every hour. It also warns that AI agents tend to open a connection per token.

facts.topic: Discovery stream: PumpPortal freshness, history, terms
facts.claim: The FAQ says the PumpPortal stream runs at 'processed' commitment and is 'typically be less than 100 msec delayed behind gRPC data' from a New York server. This latency figure is the vendor's own claim. PumpPortal provides live data only, with no historical pump.fun data. WebSockets can disconnect during server load rebalancing. The Terms of Use say PumpPortal is not affiliated with pump.fun or Raydium and reserves the right to disable access.
facts.design_relevance: Events at processed commitment can be rolled back. Reconnect logic, slot-gap backfill from another source and a fallback discovery path are needed. History must come from elsewhere.
facts.note: The FAQ says the stream is at 'processed' and 'will typically be less than 100 msec delayed behind gRPC data if you run a server in New York' (the vendor's own claim). It says PumpPortal provides 'only live trading data' and that websockets disconnect when servers rebalance load. The Terms say PumpPortal 'IS NOT AFFILIATED... WITH PUMP.FUN OR RAYDIUM' and reserve the right to disable access on breach and to restrict access at any time without notice.

facts.claim: Solana's logsSubscribe accepts 'all', 'allWithVotes' or {mentions:[pubkey]}. The mentions filter supports exactly one address, and listing more returns Invalid params. The default commitment is finalized. Each notification carries signature, err and logs.
facts.design_relevance: Watching pump.fun, PumpSwap, LaunchLab and Meteora DBC takes one subscription per program. Commitment must be set explicitly, because the default (finalized) adds latency.
facts.note: The filter accepts all, allWithVotes or mentions. A warning says mentions 'currently supports exactly one address' and more returns Invalid params. Commitment defaults to finalized. Notifications carry signature, err and logs (page references agave v3.1.8).

facts.claim: In the Agave validator, LOG_MESSAGES_BYTES_LIMIT is 10 * 1000 bytes. Past that limit the collector appends 'Log truncated' and drops further log messages.
facts.design_relevance: A decoder that relies only on log lines can miss events in large transactions. Use inner-instruction (self-CPI) event data from full transactions or gRPC as the source of truth.
facts.note: The source has `const LOG_MESSAGES_BYTES_LIMIT: usize = 10 * 1000;`. Once bytes_written >= limit, the collector pushes 'Log truncated' once and drops every later message, including the one that crossed the limit.

facts.claim: programSubscribe streams accounts owned by a program, with filters, encodings (base58, base64, base64+zstd, jsonParsed) and a default commitment of finalized. getProgramAccounts allows up to 4 filter objects (dataSize, memcmp, tokenAccountState), all of which must match. memcmp decoded data is limited to 128 bytes.
facts.design_relevance: Bonding-curve account state (reserves, complete flag) can be followed with programSubscribe and filters. Full-holder scans need a mint memcmp filter plus a dataSize or tokenAccountState filter.
facts.note: programSubscribe defaults to finalized commitment, accepts up to 4 filters that must all match, and supports base58/base64/base64+zstd/jsonParsed. The default encoding is the deprecated 'binary', so the encoding must be set explicitly. The getProgramAccounts filter table lists memcmp (decoded data limited to 128 bytes), dataSize and tokenAccountState, and 'all filter criteria' must be met. Note for the design: Token-2022 accounts with extensions are not 165 bytes, so a dataSize:165 filter misses them. tokenAccountState covers both Token and Token-2022.

facts.claim: getTokenLargestAccounts returns the 20 largest token accounts for a mint. Each entry has address, amount, decimals and uiAmount. The results are token accounts, not owner wallets.
facts.design_relevance: Top-holder concentration needs a second lookup to map each account to its owner, and must exclude the bonding-curve or pool vault accounts. Only the top 20 are visible.
facts.note: Returns up to 20 entries with address (a token account), amount, decimals, uiAmount (deprecated) and uiAmountString. No owner field is returned.

facts.claim: getSignaturesForAddress returns confirmed signatures newest-first, with a limit between 1 and 1,000 (default 1,000) and before/until cursors.
facts.design_relevance: Recent trades for a token can be backfilled by paging signatures and then fetching transactions. Each page costs extra RPC calls, so it suits gap repair rather than bulk history.
facts.note: Returns confirmed signatures newest-first. limit is 1-1,000 with default 1000, and before/until cursors exist. Commitment accepts confirmed or finalized, default finalized.

facts.claim: Solana's public mainnet endpoint (https://api.mainnet.solana.com) allows 100 requests per 10 s per IP, 40 requests per 10 s per IP for a single RPC method, 40 concurrent connections, a connection rate of 40 per 10 s, and 100 MB of data per 30 s. The docs say it is 'not intended for production applications' and that the limits may change.
facts.design_relevance: Holder scans and transaction backfill cannot run on the public RPC in production. A provider is required (pricing belongs to LD).
facts.note: Mainnet https://api.mainnet.solana.com: 100 req/10 s per IP, 40 req/10 s per IP per RPC, 40 concurrent connections, 40 connections per 10 s, 100 MB per 30 s. The page says it is 'not intended for production applications' and that limits may change. The .md URL reset the connection twice; read via the non-.md URL.

facts.claim: Yellowstone gRPC transaction filters support vote, failed, account_include (OR), account_exclude and account_required (AND), at commitment processed, confirmed or finalized. The server sends a Ping every 15 s. SubscribeDeshred streams pre-execution transactions but has no execution status, logs, inner instructions or balances.
facts.design_relevance: gRPC with account_include=[launchpad program IDs] gives full transactions with inner instructions, which suits event decoding. Deshred is earlier but cannot confirm success or decode self-CPI events.
facts.note: Transaction filters include vote, failed, account_include (any), account_exclude and account_required (all). Commitment can be processed, confirmed or finalized. The server sends a Ping every 15s. Deshred lacks execution status, logs, inner instructions and balances. Missing caveat: the README says the open-source yellowstone-grpc-geyser server returns UNIMPLEMENTED for SubscribeDeshred, so only some providers offer it. Servers can also cap filter sizes (config example: account_include_max 10).

facts.claim: create_v2 creates a new Token-2022 mint (program TokenzQdBNbLqP5VEhdkAS6EPFLC1PHnBqCXEpPxuEb) with decimals = 6. It takes an optional is_holder_reward argument and rejects is_cashback_enabled=[true] because cashback is deprecated. CreateEvent now includes quote_mint, creator_fee_bps, is_mayhem_mode and is_holder_reward.
facts.design_relevance: Holder scans for these coins must query the Token-2022 program, not only SPL Token. Token-metadata parsing must handle Token-2022.

The IDL CreateEvent fields include quote_mint, creator_fee_bps, is_mayhem_mode and is_holder_reward, plus token_program and virtual_quote_reserves.

facts.claim: The pump.fun README announces new instructions (buy_v2, sell_v2, buy_exact_quote_in_v2) that support non-SOL quote mints. BondingCurve fields were renamed (virtual_sol_reserves to virtual_quote_reserves, real_sol_reserves to real_quote_reserves) and a quote_mint field was added. USDC-paired coins cannot be traded with the legacy instructions. TradeEvent carries quote_mint, quote_amount and virtual/real quote reserves alongside the legacy sol_* fields. The undated README section says USDC would be added 'next week'.
facts.as_of: 2026-09-29 commit; launch date of USDC pairs not stated
facts.design_relevance: Prices and PnL must be computed in the quote mint actually used. Hard-coding SOL as the quote will misprice USDC-paired coins.
facts.note: The README confirms the new instructions, the renames, the quote_mint field, 'Trading USDC-paired coins will not be possible with the legacy instructions', and 'We will add USDC next week. Exact Date and time TBH'. The TradeEvent IDL has both sol_* and quote_* fields. Extra detail: BondingCurve.quote_mint is Pubkey::default() (all zeros, not the wSOL mint) for every SOL-paired coin, while the v2 instructions expect the wSOL mint to be passed.

facts.claim: PumpSwap Pool.virtual_quote_reserves is an i128. Effective quote reserves = pool_quote_token_account.amount + virtual_quote_reserves, and from September 30 the virtual term may be negative. Pump guarantees the sum never overflows and is never negative. BuyEvent and SellEvent logs include virtual_quote_reserves.
facts.design_relevance: Post-migration price and liquidity must use signed effective reserves. Pricing from the raw vault balance alone is wrong.
facts.note: The README says 'Starting September 30, Pool::virtual_quote_reserves can be negative', always i128, and that the sum is guaranteed never to overflow and never to be negative. In the IDL, Pool.virtual_quote_reserves is i128 and BuyEvent/SellEvent carry virtual_quote_reserves (i128).

facts.claim: The BondingCurve 'complete' flag becomes true at the end of the buy that completes the curve. migrate(user, mint) is permissionless and idempotent, and moves a completed curve (complete == true and real_token_reserves == 0) into a PumpSwap pool. The LP tokens received from PumpSwap are burnt.
facts.design_relevance: Graduation detection can key off CompleteEvent or the complete flag plus the migrate/CreatePoolEvent. The state machine should allow a gap between completion and migration.
facts.note: 'complete'... is set to true at the end of a buy when real_token_reserves == 0. migrate(user, mint) is idempotent and permissionless, and the LP tokens from PumpSwap are burnt. The doc also says BondingCurve accounts written before later fields existed are shorter, and decoders should read the missing trailing fields as 0/false/default.

facts.claim: pump buy, buy_v2 and create_v2 take event_authority and program accounts, the Anchor event-CPI pattern. Dune's spellbook pump.fun model decodes TradeEvent from solana.instruction_calls data starting with 0xe445a52e51cb9a1d (followed by the event discriminator), i.e. from self-CPI inner instructions.
facts.design_relevance: Reading events needs a source with inner instructions (full transactions, gRPC, Parsed Streams), not just logsSubscribe. The 'inner instruction' reading is inferred from the IDL accounts and Dune's decoder.
facts.note: buy, buy_v2 and create_v2 all end with event_authority and program accounts. Dune filters instruction_calls on the 16-byte prefix 0xe445a52e51cb9a1d + bddb7fd34ee661ee. The second half matches the IDL TradeEvent discriminator [189,219,127,211,78,230,97,238]. Reading this as a self-CPI is still an inference, as the claim says.

facts.claim: Parsed Streams (parsedTransactionSubscribe) delivers decoded transactions at confirmed commitment (votes excluded), decodes 3,600+ programs including Pump.fun and PumpSwap, and filters on programs, instructionNames, accounts.include/roles, includeCpi and includeFailed. It is on all plans including Free, at 1 credit per delivered event, metered from 2026-09-24 (earlier users from 2026-10-01). It is served only at wss://beta.helius-rpc.com/?api-key=..., with 401 for a bad key and 429 at the connection cap. The Pump.fun guide's 'currently only available on wss://fs-beta.helius-rpc.com' sentence refers to the describeProgram discovery call, not the stream. The same guide's subscription code connects to wss://beta.helius-rpc.com.
facts.design_relevance: This is a decoded discovery stream that runs on a free plan, but every event costs a credit. Confirmed commitment is slower than processed. The host must be configurable.
facts.original_claim: Helius Parsed Streams (parsedTransactionSubscribe over WebSocket) pushes decoded transactions at confirmed commitment. It decodes through an IDL catalog of 3,600+ programs, including Pump.fun and PumpSwap, and filters on programs, instructionNames, accounts, includeCpi and includeFailed. It is available on all plans including Free, at 1 credit per delivered event, with metering from 2026-09-24. The overview gives the host as wss://beta.helius-rpc.com, with 401 for a bad key and 429 at the connection cap. The Pump.fun-mints guide instead says the stream is 'currently only available on wss://fs-beta.helius-rpc.com', and filters on create and create_v2.

facts.claim: LaserStream WebSocket standard Solana methods are available on all plans. Helius extensions (transactionSubscribe, enhanced accountSubscribe) need the Developer, Business or Professional plan. Both are metered at 2 credits per 0.1 MB of uncompressed data. LaserStream gRPC on mainnet needs Business or Professional and costs 2 credits per 0.1 MB, with up to 48-hour historical replay.
facts.design_relevance: Raw firehose subscriptions are billed by bytes, so tight filters matter. gRPC replay helps gap repair but needs a higher tier (LD prices tiers).
facts.note: Standard LaserStream WSS methods: all plans. Extensions (transactionSubscribe, enhanced accountSubscribe): Developer, Business and Professional. Both cost 2 credits per 0.1 MB uncompressed. Mainnet gRPC is Business/Professional at 2 credits per 0.1 MB (devnet on all plans). llms.txt says 'up to 48-hour historical replay'.

facts.claim: Helius webhook events cost 1 credit each, charged whether or not the endpoint processes them. Deliveries may be retried, so duplicates are possible. Raw Transaction Webhooks have lower latency than Enhanced ones, and Parsed Streams succeeds Enhanced Transaction Webhooks. Webhooks with a 95% or higher failure rate are auto-disabled: over 7 days on paid plans, over 24 hours on Free.
facts.design_relevance: Webhooks need an always-up public HTTPS receiver and idempotent dedupe by signature. They suit low-rate events such as graduations more than per-trade streams.
facts.note: Each event costs 1 credit whether or not the endpoint processes it. Retries may produce duplicates. Raw webhooks have lower latency. Parsed Streams succeeds Enhanced Transaction Webhooks. facts.topic: pump.fun decoder: SOL quote_mint sentinel and short legacy accounts
facts.claim: BondingCurve.quote_mint is Pubkey::default() (all zeros) for every coin created to date and for every SOL-quoted coin. When calling buy_v2, sell_v2 or buy_exact_quote_in_v2 on those coins, integrators must pass the wSOL mint So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112. BondingCurve accounts written before later fields were added are shorter, and missing trailing fields must be read as 0/false/Pubkey::default().

facts.topic: SPL Token mint authority and freeze authority
facts.claim: In the SPL Token program the Mint account (82 bytes) holds mint_authority: COption<Pubkey> (if none, supply is fixed and no further tokens can be minted), supply: u64, decimals: u8, is_initialized: bool and freeze_authority: COption<Pubkey>. The FreezeAccount instruction freezes an initialized token account using the mint's freeze_authority, if one is set.
facts.design_relevance: Two of the token gate's inputs are mint_authority (more tokens can be minted) and freeze_authority (the classic honeypot: you can buy but not sell). Both can be read directly from RPC account data, so no paid service is needed.
facts.note: The Mint struct and LEN=82 match, and so does the comment 'If no mint authority is present then the mint has a fixed supply'. The FreezeAccount doc reads 'Freeze an Initialized account using the Mint's freeze_authority (if set)'.

facts.claim: A 2026 Solana rug-pull study describes 'Freeze Authority Abuse' as follows: a frozen token account cannot perform any token operation, transfers and swaps included, 'resulting in a situation where the token can be purchased but cannot be sold'. Of the study's 76,469 pipeline-labelled rug tokens, 461 were Freeze Authority Abuse cases.
facts.design_relevance: A non-null freeze authority should be a hard reject for meme tokens. A pre-trade sell simulation cannot catch a freeze that happens after entry.
facts.note: The quote matches exactly, as does '461 Freeze Authority Abuse tokens'. v2 is dated 31 May 2026. The Freeze Authority Abuse label also requires that a FreezeAccount instruction was actually executed against a user account.

facts.claim: An SPL token account has one delegate: COption<Pubkey> field and a delegated_amount: u64. The Approve instruction gives a delegate 'authority over tokens on behalf of the source account's owner', and Revoke removes it. Token-2022 also has an AuthorityType::AccountOwner that SetAuthority can change, plus a CloseAccount authority.
facts.design_relevance: The bot should never sign Approve or SetAuthority. It should regularly check that its own token accounts have no delegate, owner change or close authority, and it should screen any transaction built by a third party, such as an aggregator API response, for these instructions before signing.
facts.note: The delegate and delegated_amount fields, the Approve doc text and Revoke all match. The Token-2022 AuthorityType includes AccountOwner ('Owner of a given token account') and CloseAccount.

facts.claim: The official Solana Token-2022 extension list contains 28 entries: Uninitialized, TransferFeeConfig, TransferFeeAmount, MintCloseAuthority, ConfidentialTransferMint, ConfidentialTransferAccount, DefaultAccountState, ImmutableOwner, MemoTransfer, NonTransferable ('tokens from this mint can't be transferred'), InterestBearingConfig, CpiGuard, PermanentDelegate, NonTransferableAccount, TransferHook, TransferHookAccount, ConfidentialTransferFeeConfig, ConfidentialTransferFeeAmount, MetadataPointer, TokenMetadata, GroupPointer, TokenGroup, GroupMemberPointer, TokenGroupMember, ConfidentialMintBurn, ScaledUiAmount, Pausable and PausableAccount.
facts.design_relevance: This is the base list for the extension allow/deny policy. Pump.fun mints legitimately use MetadataPointer and TokenMetadata (see TH-16), so the gate has to judge each extension separately instead of rejecting every Token-2022 token.
facts.note: The ExtensionType code block on that page lists exactly these 28 variants, ending at PausableAccount. However, the same docs site's sidebar has a separate 'Permissioned Burn' extension page, so the code block is not the full set the docs cover.
